businesses.description: Metallurgical coal for steelmaking and thermal coal. CSX and NS built their networks around this corridor. Moves to Virginia/Baltimore ports for export or west to Midwest steel mills.
Southern terminus of the Mississippi River industrial corridor. Grain and chemicals transfer barge-to-ocean vessel. Connected to Gulf Intracoastal Waterway. CN, CSX, UP rail access.
BNSF intermodal — ~600K container lifts annually, 16 double-stack trains daily. All-freight airport, FTZ, US Customs on site. UP also provides carload service to industrial tenants.
6,500-acre inland port complex near Joliet, IL. BNSF and UP railheads. 10M+ sq ft of distribution space. Located on CN's EJ&E bypass route — freight avoids downtown Chicago congestion entirely.

25% of all US rail freight touches Chicago. Every Class I railroad converges here. Historically 24-36 hrs to hand off one car between carriers. CREATE Program modernizing infrastructure. CN's EJ&E bypass — Waukegan to Joliet ring — is the only completed Class I bypass in North America.
One of 5 CPKC intermodal terminals in the US. Sits on former KCS mainline connecting Gulf of Mexico to Kansas City and Canada. Key node on the only single-railroad US-Canada-Mexico route.
175,873 containers moved in 2023 — up 26% year over year. Built specifically to serve BMW Spartanburg plant. NS rail connection to Port of Charleston. Auto parts inbound, finished vehicles outbound.
Largest petrochemical manufacturing corridor in the world — Houston Ship Channel to Baton Rouge. Tank cars and covered hoppers distribute chemicals and plastics to every corner of North America.

Major forest products import and export hub. Paper rolls from Finland and Sweden inbound. Pulp from Brazil. Southeast lumber and pulp outbound. CSX and NS connections. 240,000 sq ft on-dock covered warehouse.

businesses.company_name: Laredo TX (US/Mexico Rail Gateway via CPKC)
businesses.description: Primary US-Mexico rail crossing. CPKC's most strategic asset post-merger. Automotive parts, beer (Modelo/Corona), grain, manufactured goods, and steel coils cross daily. Gateway on the only single-railroad US-Canada-Mexico route in existence.
Largest port complex in North America. Asian imports enter here and move east by UP and BNSF double-stack intermodal trains. Western gateway for all import container flows.

Ohio River transfer point. 23,000-ft double-loop rail track receives full 120-car unit trains. Entire train off-loaded in one 8-hour shift directly into barges. Primary commodities: coal, grain, fertilizer, potash.
5th largest inland port in the US. Mississippi River barge access + 5 Class I railroads + interstate highway convergence + FedEx air hub. Every freight mode touches Memphis.
Center of gravity for US grain — corn and soybeans move to Gulf export elevators or east to ports. Steel from Indiana mills feeds auto plants. Every Class I railroad converges on Chicago.
Wheat, corn, canola, and Bakken crude oil. One of the most freight-dense rail corridors in North America. BNSF dominant.

#1 US port for autos, farm and construction machinery, imported forest products, sugar, and aluminum. CSX and NS Class I connections. Seagirt Marine Terminal and Dundalk — 570 acres of cargo handling.
National leader in break bulk cargo volume. Dominates oil and gas equipment, steel pipe, wind turbine components, heavy lift project cargo. All Class I rail carriers accessible via Ship Channel.

businesses.company_name: Port of Mobile (#1 US Forest Products)
businesses.description: Largest break bulk forest products port in the United States. Dockside rail facility — direct car-to-vessel transfer. CN is primary rail carrier from the Southeast pine belt. Also serves steel and chemicals. Website: alports.com

97 miles inland on the Mississippi River — unique convergence of river barge, rail, and ocean vessel. All 6 Class I railroads serve this port. Iron and steel imports, chemicals, project cargo, grain export.
Third-busiest US port by volume. Enormous inbound container flows move inland by rail and truck. Scrap metal moves outbound to Midwest mills. CSX and NS serve the region.
372% surge in break bulk driven by offshore wind — tower sections, nacelles, turbine blades. CSX and NS connections. Fastest growing break bulk segment in the US driven by the energy buildout.
Largest coal-producing region in North America. BNSF and UP run dedicated unit trains east to Midwest power plants and west to Pacific Coast export terminals.
World's largest potash reserves. CP/CPKC's most important single commodity. Moves south by rail to US fertilizer markets.

businesses.company_name: Savannah Garden City Terminal (SE Intermodal Gateway)
businesses.description: 3rd largest container port in the US and fastest growing. Foreign auto plants — BMW, Mercedes, Hyundai — generate massive rail car flows. CSX and NS connections. Expanding capacity through 2040.

Northwest Seaport Alliance — break bulk, containers, project cargo, autos. Forest products moving outbound from Pacific Northwest timber country. BNSF and UP connections. Canadian and US grain export via Vancouver.
MS, AL, GA, SC pine belt produces wood pulp, cellulose rolls, kraft liner board, and lumber. CN (former Illinois Central) and CSX/NS move product to Gulf and Atlantic break bulk terminals.

15 barge transfer facilities — highest handling capacity anywhere on the Mississippi River. Connected to BNSF, CN, CSX, NS, and UP. 32M+ tons/year. Grain arrives by rail from the Corn Belt, loads onto barges, moves south to Gulf export terminals.

Western terminus for Canadian and US Prairie grain exports to Asia. CN and CP compete for this corridor. State-of-the-art grain handling. Pacific gateway for North American agricultural and potash exports.
CN and CP primary US-Canada crossing point. Canadian grain, potash, and forest products move south. Import containers move north. Western gateway for trans-Pacific trade flows in both directions.

businesses.source_note: Drax wood-pellet mill in Bastrop, LA — ships pellets via ALM shortline to UP interchange in Collinston, then to Port of Greater Baton Rouge for export to UK; ~10,000 carloads/year per G&W
Morning Star is the world's largest tomato processor; Williams CA facility served by California Northern (G&W); also Los Banos plant (separate)

businesses.company_name: Columbus & Ohio River Rail Road customer base
businesses.source_note: C&OR (G&W) serves food/consumer-goods/paper shippers in Eastern Ohio — Coshocton hub on NS interchange
P&G Cincinnati manufacturing complex — served by Indiana & Ohio Railway (G&W subsidiary) for sanitizer feedstock during 2020 demand surge

businesses.company_name: Tyson Foods Pittsburg Poultry Feed Mill
businesses.source_note: Tyson Foods mega poultry feed mill in Pittsburg, OK — served by Kiamichi Railroad (G&W subsidiary)
Maryland Midland (G&W) serves Carroll County stone/salt operations; key inbound for road maintenance materials
Georgia-Pacific Wauna tissue/paper mill near Clatskanie, OR — served by P&W shortline; G&W published case study during COVID-19 demand surge

businesses.company_name: Mega Rail Terminal at Port of Savannah
businesses.source_note: Savannah Port Terminal Railroad (G&W) provides switching at Mega Rail Terminal — Garden City Terminal, NS + CSXT dual-served intermodal hub
Tomahawk Railway combined-rail/warehousing operation in Tomahawk, WI — serves Wisconsin Northwoods forest-products mills; CN interchange
